prompt:
Professional film character reference sheet, photoreal, four equal vertical panels side by side on one seamless neutral mid-grey studio backdrop, identical soft key light from camera-left with a subtle warm orange rim light and cool blue fill, 35mm film photograph with fine grain, muted palette. No text, no labels, no captions, no watermark.

The SAME man appears in all four panels: Cass Varro, a freight pilot in the year 2083, late 30s, lean build, weathered sun-damaged skin with faint freckling and fine lines, three-day stubble going grey at the chin, short dark hair with the left side of his head shaved close, a small brushed-steel neural jack port set into the skin just behind his LEFT ear with a little scar tissue around it, tired hooded eyes, a wry lopsided half-smile like he is already talking his way out of something. Wearing a faded rust-orange flight jacket with patched elbows and a peeling cargo-union shoulder patch, over a grey thermal henley.

Panel 1 (far left): head-and-shoulders portrait, facing camera straight on, neutral expression.
Panel 2: head-and-shoulders portrait, three-quarter view turned to his right, wry half-smile.
Panel 3: head-and-shoulders portrait, strict side profile facing screen-right so the LEFT side of his head is visible, showing the shaved side and the steel neural jack port behind the ear.
Panel 4 (far right): full-body standing shot head to boots, facing camera, relaxed slouch, utility belt with a battered rugged tablet holstered and a coiled tether line clipped at the hip, worn cargo trousers, scuffed work boots.

Practical working-class spacer, long-haul trucker energy, not a soldier or hero. Real skin texture, pores, no makeup, no cartoon, no CGI look.
